prompts:
This is an instructional notebook. It is notebook 5, the first notebook of part 2 (classification) of the course "Tabular Foundation Models with TabICL".

Content: builds intuition on `predict_proba` with 2D toy data, comparing `LogisticRegression`, `HistGradientBoostingClassifier` (HGBT) and TabICL (`TabAPIClassifier` with `n_estimators=1`). Probability maps are drawn with `DecisionBoundaryDisplay` and a diverging colormap: blue for a low probability of the positive class, red for a high one, white at 0.5, darker meaning more sure; a dashed line marks 0.5. Maps extend beyond the data to show extrapolation. The inductive bias, introduced in the learning curve notebook, becomes visible: logistic regression gives a straight boundary (sigmoid of a linear function), HGBT boxes aligned with the axes (trees split one feature at a time), TabICL smooth curves (its prior mixes many kinds of relationships). Models are compared with the log loss, which heavily penalizes a confident wrong probability, over 25 shared splits of a repeated stratified k-fold, with per-split differences.

Results of the reference run. Two moons: logistic regression draws a straight boundary with a wide unsure strip, HGBT a staircase, TabICL a curve following the gap; away from the data each model extends its own kind of relationship, including a pale red HGBT box in an empty corner. A dark colour means sure, not right. TabICL has the lowest mean log loss; logistic regression is clearly worse (difference about three times its standard deviation); HGBT vs TabICL varies a lot across splits. Imbalanced XOR (two small positive blobs of 8 rows): logistic regression cannot represent it and predicts about the positive share everywhere (16 out of 116); HGBT isolates the blobs in sharp boxes, TabICL with curves; both are sure in empty corners. TabICL has the lowest mean log loss, but the difference with HGBT is about one standard deviation, since a test fold holds only 3 or 4 positives. Rare class along a sine band (25 positives out of 400, true probability at most 0.5, known since the data is synthetic): HGBT draws small dark red boxes with probabilities near 1, TabICL a faint ridge mostly below 0.5; TabICL's log loss comes closest to the true probability's, which no model reaches.

Place in the course: first classification notebook. The next notebooks check on real card fraud what HGBT's confident boxes cost (calibration, decision thresholds); questions on calibration or thresholds get a short answer and a pointer there. Related scikit-learn course material: logistic regression (Linear Models), decision trees and their boundaries (Decision Trees), log loss and classification metrics (Evaluating Model Performance).
